articles.title: Neurons++: A Unified Visual-Stream Framework for Image and Video Reconstruction from fMRI with Neural-to-Visual Interpretability
articles.selectionReason: Open full-text paper; topic brain_computer_interface; quality signal passed; application scenario is clear.

paperCard.problem: 现有的脑活动（fMRI）解码方法有两个毛病：一是图像重建和视频重建被当成两件互不相干的事，图像模型的“空间与物体语义”经验帮不到视频；二是生成出来的画面虽然好看，但可能主要是生成模型的想象，并不真正对应大脑活动，而且中间过程难以追踪。
paperCard.method: 作者把图像看作“单帧视觉流”、视频看作“多帧视觉流”，统一成一个问题来建模。先用大量“图像—fMRI”数据做多被试预训练，得到一个稳定的空间语义起点，再针对每个被试分别微调图像和视频任务。解码过程用一个“串行视觉解耦器”，按顺序把脑信号转成物体结构、物体语义、场景语言描述和粗略的时间变化，再交给生成模型出图或出视频。
paperCard.difference: 之前的方法要么只做视频、要么只做图像，两类任务各用一套设计；而且脑信号里的低层结构、高层语义、时间动态往往是被隐式对齐或并行拼接的独立条件，看不出哪一层脑信息贡献了什么。NEURONS++把图像和视频放在同一个“视觉流”框架下，并把并行的任务条件改成串行、有先后层次的解码链，让“神经—视觉”的对应关系可追溯。
paperCard.innovation: 三点：一是提出“视觉流”这一统一设定，把静态图像和动态视频重建串起来；二是提出受脑皮层启发的串行视觉解耦器，把空间、语义、语言、时间线索组织成层层递进的通路；三是做了delta-fMRI扰动、脑区（ROI）屏蔽和ROI放大三类实验，用证据说明解码内容是“方向可控的”、对刺激相关的皮层活动敏感、并且能通过干预特定脑区来调节语义结果。
paperCard.implementation: 实现分三步走。第一步是编码：用脑编码模块把体素（voxel，fMRI里最小测量单元）响应映射到与CLIP视觉/文本模型对齐的向量空间。第二步是串行解耦：依次产出关键物体分割、概念识别、场景描述、模糊视频等线索，构成从空间到语义到语言再到时间的逐级表示。第三步是统一推理：用这些线索驱动扩散模型（diffusion model，一类通过逐步去噪生成图像的生成模型），单帧出图像、多帧出视频（实现中一个片段默认6帧）。训练上先做多被试图像-fMRI预训练，再做被试特定微调。
paperCard.applications: 可用于脑机接口与认知神经科学研究：帮助理解人脑如何表征视觉内容；面向严重运动障碍患者的沟通辅助（用想象画面重建内容）；也可作为检验生成模型是否“忠于脑信号”的可解释性工具，以及脑区功能与视觉语义对应关系的研究手段。

BOLD信号：fMRI测到的血氧依赖信号，变化慢，所以视频解码的时间分辨率受限。
视觉流：本文的说法，把图像看作单帧、视频看作多帧，统一成一条时间上的画面序列。
串行视觉解耦器：把脑信号按顺序拆成空间、语义、语言、时间四类线索的解码模块。
扩散模型：通过不断去噪逐步生成图像或视频的生成模型。
CLIP：能把图像和文字映射到同一向量空间的多模态模型，常用来做语义对齐。
ROI：感兴趣脑区，这里指对重建结果做屏蔽或放大实验的特定皮层区域。
delta-fMRI扰动：人为改变脑信号后观察重建结果是否按方向变化，用来检验因果性。
体素：fMRI数据里的最小三维测量单元，类似大脑图像的“像素”。

Recent generative decoding methods can reconstruct plausible images and videos, but visual plausibility alone does not ensure that the output is faithfully grounded in brain activity. In this work, we propose NEURONS++, a visual- stream fMRI reconstruction framework for both static image and dynamic video reconstruction.

en.highlight: NEURONS++ achieves state-of-the-art video reconstruction and competitive image reconstruction across standard benchmarks.
en.summary: This paper proposes NEURONS++, which unifies fMRI-to-image and fMRI-to-video reconstruction under a single 'fMRI-to-visual-stream' formulation: one frame means an image, multiple frames mean a video. A cortex-inspired Serial Visual Decoupler progressively turns brain activity into spatial, semantic, language-level and temporal cues that drive a generative model. What makes it worth reading is that beyond visual fidelity, it tests whether reconstructions are truly grounded in brain activity via delta-fMRI perturbation, ROI ablation and ROI amplification.
en.failureAnalysis: Only the abstract and introduction are available here, so the claimed state-of-the-art and competitive results cannot be independently verified from the provided content. The method also still requires subject-specific and dataset-specific adaptation, leaving generalization to real brain-computer-interface settings unproven.
en.title: Neurons++: A Unified Visual-Stream Framework for Image and Video Reconstruction from fMRI with Neural-to-Visual Interpretability

paperCard.problem: Existing fMRI decoding methods have two weaknesses: image and video reconstruction are developed as separate settings, so image models' spatial and object-semantic supervision cannot help dynamic decoding; and visually plausible outputs may be driven by generative priors rather than faithfully reflecting brain activity, with no traceable path from neural signal to output.
paperCard.method: The authors formulate images as single-frame visual streams and videos as multi-frame visual streams under one problem setting. Multi-subject image-fMRI pretraining provides a stable spatial-semantic initialization, followed by subject-specific fine-tuning for image and video tasks. A Serial Visual Decoupler progressively converts brain signals into spatial object structure, object-level semantics, scene-level language and coarse temporal appearance, which then drive image or video generation.
paperCard.difference: Earlier work either handled video only or images only, with separate designs, and typically aligned or aggregated neural cues implicitly or in parallel as independent conditions, making it hard to trace which neural level contributed what. NEURONS++ connects both tasks in a shared visual-stream formulation and replaces parallel task conditioning with a serial, brain-inspired, hierarchical decoding chain.
paperCard.innovation: Three contributions: a new visual-stream formulation linking static image and dynamic video reconstruction; a brain-inspired Serial Visual Decoupler organizing spatial, semantic, language-level and temporal cues into a progressive neural-to-visual hierarchy; and experimental evidence that decoded content is directionally controllable, sensitive to stimulus-relevant cortical activity, and modulated by region-specific neural interventions.
paperCard.implementation: Three steps. First, a brain encoding module maps voxel responses into visual and textual embeddings aligned with vision-language models such as CLIP. Second, the Serial Visual Decoupler produces key object segmentation, concept recognition, scene description and blurry video cues in sequence. Third, a unified visual-stream inference pipeline uses these cues to drive a diffusion model for single-frame images or multi-frame videos (six frames per clip by default). Training is two-stage: multi-subject image-fMRI pretraining, then subject-specific adaptation.
paperCard.applications: Brain-computer interfaces and cognitive neuroscience: understanding how the brain represents visual content; communication assistance for patients with severe motor impairment via imagined visual decoding; and use as an interpretability tool to check whether generative outputs are truly grounded in brain signals, as well as for studying brain-region-to-semantics correspondences.
technicalTerms: fMRI: functional magnetic resonance imaging, which indirectly measures brain activity via blood oxygenation changes.
BOLD signal: the blood-oxygen-level-dependent signal measured by fMRI; it is slow, limiting temporal resolution for video decoding.
visual stream: the paper's notion of treating an image as a single frame and a video as multiple frames in one temporal sequence.
Serial Visual Decoupler: a decoding module that sequentially decomposes brain signals into spatial, semantic, language-level and temporal cues.
diffusion model: a generative model that produces images or videos by gradually denoising random noise.
CLIP: a multimodal model mapping images and text into a shared embedding space, used here for semantic alignment.
ROI: region of interest; here, specific cortical areas ablated or amplified in experiments.
delta-fMRI perturbation: artificially altering brain signals to see whether reconstructions change directionally, testing causality.
voxel: the smallest three-dimensional measurement unit in fMRI data, akin to a pixel of the brain image.
NSD: the Natural Scenes Dataset, a large-scale brain imaging dataset commonly used for fMRI-to-image reconstruction.

articles.title: sirioberati/Genjustsu-Open-Source-Workflow
articles.selectionReason: AI source passed freshness and evidence-chain gate: GitHub + Community signal
articles.summary: 这个 GitHub 项目提供开源 AI 视频替换工作流，把深度图、SAM 分割、面部网格和音频处理组合起来，用 Seedance 替换角色或物体。它还带有本地 Web UI，用于准备输入、检查遮罩、预览生成并导出保留原始音频的视频。项目已有 729 星和近期公开活动，值得关注其把多种视觉模型串成可操作流水线的工程路径。
articles.failureAnalysis: 该工作流依赖 Seedance 以及 SAM、面部网格等多个组件，推理成本和算力开销可能很高，普通用户难以日常使用。视频替换涉及肖像、版权与深度伪造合规风险，若缺少授权机制或内容溯源，可能限制分发和商业化。工程上，掩码、深度和音频同步的稳定性需要大量真实场景验证，否则输出质量波动会削弱实际需求。开源项目还要面对维护、文档和集成成本，729 星不足以证明付费或规模化采用。

en.highlight: Combine depth maps, SAM segmentation, face meshes, and audio processing to replace characters and objects with Seedance.
en.summary: This GitHub project offers an open-source AI video replacement workflow that combines depth maps, SAM segmentation, face meshes, and audio processing to replace characters or objects with Seedance. It also includes a local web UI for preparing inputs, reviewing masks, previewing generations, and exporting with original audio. With 729 stars and recent public activity, it is worth watching as an engineering path for chaining multiple vision models into a usable pipeline.
en.failureAnalysis: The workflow depends on Seedance plus multiple vision components, so inference cost and hardware requirements may keep it out of everyday use. Video replacement also raises portrait rights, copyright, and deepfake compliance risks, while mask, depth, and audio synchronization still need real-world validation.
